I'm not sure 400 is the best error code... isn't a 500 better?  If you're satisfied with a 400 or would prefer that Modeshape return a more apt error, that's fine too, but if we put just a couple lines of code in here (either to return the root cause "no more space" or even to log it) it might save a future fedora user a lot of time debugging.   After the failure, the temp file is deleted, so there's no obvious indication that disk space was an issue.

When uploading a large file Modeshape stores it in the temp directory.  If there is insufficient space, a 400 error is returned with no useful message.  It is especially difficult to debug this error since there is no stack trace (no matter how much logging is enabled) and because, non-intuitively, fedora 4 writes to the temp space, which may be on a different volume than the storage space fedora is configured to use.
The following stack trace was derived by using a modified version of fedora 4.
org.modeshape.jcr.value.ValueFormatException: Error converting InputStream to a BinaryValue
Caused by: org.modeshape.jcr.value.binary.BinaryStoreException: java.io.IOException: No space left on device
Caused by: java.io.IOException: No space left on device

fields.summary: Fedora 4 returns a 400 error when uploading a file larger than the available space in the temp directory.

comments.body: Michael Durbin, is this not a MODE ticket? Can we move it over there and close it WON'T-FIX?

I'm not sure 400 is the best error code... isn't a 500 better? If you're satisfied with a 400 or would prefer that Modeshape return a more apt error, that's fine too, but if we put just a couple lines of code in here (either to return the root cause "no more space" or even to log it) it might save a future fedora user a lot of time debugging. After the failure, the temp file is deleted, so there's no obvious indication that disk space was an issue.

Okay, if you're confident you know how to detect this condition, I don't think anyone would be unhappy with more precise diagnostics . One thing to watch out for is that some folks will not want to publish details of their filesystems in cases like this, so whatever you do needs to be config'able. I would probably go for 507 (Insufficient Storage) as per that link to WebDAV extensions.

It is especially difficult to debug this error since there is no stack trace (no matter how much logging is enabled) and because, non-intuitively, fedora 4 writes to the temp space, which may be on a different volume than the storage space fedora is configured to use.
